headline: Timeshare strength offsets exchange business decline
summary_short: Travel + Leisure's Q2 2026 revenue rose 4.4% y/y (+10.6% q/q) to $1,063M and diluted EPS grew 6.2% y/y to $1.72, as Vacation Ownership tour and pricing gains offset continued declines in the Travel and Membership exchange business.
summary_long: Revenue rose 4.4% y/y to $1,063M: Vacation Ownership net VOI sales grew $48M on higher VPGs (+2.1%) and tours (+1.4%), while Travel and Membership revenue fell $10M as Exchange transactions dropped 13.4% and Travel Club's lower-commission mix pressured revenue per transaction. Net income rose 0.9% y/y to $109M despite $20M more marketing spend and $6M of resort-optimization write-downs; diluted EPS grew faster (+6.2%) on a 4.7% smaller diluted share count from buybacks. TNL repurchased $175M of stock and paid $78M of dividends YTD, leaving a $1,019M stockholders' deficit. For 2026, management guided total capex to $90-100M and Vacation Ownership development spending to $200-230M. Post-quarter, TNL closed the Yes& Vacations deal and agreed to buy Spinnaker Resorts for $150M.

drivers.explanation: Management cited the strength and efficiency of its vacation ownership sales process, driven by high-quality tours and 2025 resort-optimization savings, against continued exchange-member headwinds at Travel and Membership.

Vacation Ownership net VOI sales rose on higher VPGs and tours plus higher property-management and travel-package revenue; partly offset by a Travel and Membership decline from a lower-commission, Travel-Club-heavy transaction mix.

Higher segment revenue and a $21M drop in developer obligations from resort optimization were partly offset by $20M more marketing spend, $14M higher G&A, and $6M of resort-optimization inventory write-downs.
EPS grew faster than net income because diluted share count fell 4.7% y/y on continued buybacks under the $7.75B-cap repurchase program.

The stockholders' deficit widened over the first half of 2026 primarily on $175M of share repurchases and $76-78M of dividends, partially offset by net income and stock-based compensation; the release frames this as an H1-2026-vs-year-end comparison rather than a strict y/y one.
Share count fell as the company repurchased 2.4 million shares for $175M year-to-date under its ongoing buyback program.
